verdict.rationale: Neon documents the project-per-user/agent pattern as a first-class workload. Platforms can manage tens of thousands, and in some cases millions, of projects through the Neon API, with creation, configuration and cleanup automated and no compute charge for idle databases. The Management API (with an OpenAPI spec), the MCP project/branch lifecycle tools, and the branch TTLs in neon.ts provide the programmatic fleet management. Missing for 10: concrete pricing evidence for cost at thousands of projects (the only figure is a '100 projects' plan line), and independent or hands-on corroboration of fleet-scale provisioning.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can cheaply create thousands of isolated databases — one per agent, tenant, or preview — and manage the fleet programmatically

citations.quote: Neon supports a project-per-user model at large scale. Platforms can manage tens of thousands ( in some cases, millions) of projects programmatically through the Neon API.
Project creation, configuration, and cleanup are fully automated, and because Neon resources are ephemeral by design, idle databases don't incur ongoing compute overhead.
impressed at how quickly databases become available
